summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson was admitted for observation following a scheduled ERCP during which the initial biliary stent was removed and two new stents were placed due to a persistent 5 mm benign stricture at the biliary anastomosis. He developed mild right and mid-abdominal pain post-procedure, prompting admission to the transplant surgery service. His pain improved overnight, he remained afebrile, passed flatus, and tolerated a regular diet. Labs showed stable liver function and no signs of pancreatitis. He was discharged home with instructions to continue immunosuppressive and supportive medications, a short course of ciprofloxacin, and close follow-up with the transplant clinic for monitoring and future stent management.
problems: Surgical operation with anastomosis, bypass, or graft, with natural or artificial tissues used as implant causing abnormal patient reaction, or later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of operation
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of liver
Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
